sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: An evergreen subshrub of western Europe, about 20–60 cm tall. It grows in dry, acidic heathland and other open ground.

sections.title: Leaves and flowering
sections.text: Its tiny, narrow leaves are often arranged in whorls of three. In summer, the branches carry clusters of purple or magenta bells; this species illustrates the diversity of the genus Erica.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable food use is established in the sources consulted.
